title: Shoulders of Giants — Neuropharmacology & Bioenergetics: Nicotinic Allostery, SARM1/NAMPT & Rescuing Axons After Blast TBI & Metabolic Stress

teenKit.tldr: Patients with schizophrenia chain-smoke at massive rates because nicotine accidentally fixes a microscopic chemical glitch in their brain's attention circuits. Meanwhile, cutting-edge science is uncovering how to save damaged brain cells from self-destructing after physical trauma.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how invisible biochemical math errors control our focus and neuron survival completely changes how we treat mental illness and traumatic brain injuries.
keyTakeaways: Up to 90% of individuals with schizophrenia smoke heavily because nicotine unconsciously acts as a self-medication tool for broken cognitive circuitry.
Neurons make literal physical decisions to either repair themselves or trigger programmed self-destruction based on cellular energy levels like NAD+.
Advanced diagnostics can spot hidden, subclinical brain and vision damage after blast injuries before permanent cell death sets in.

vocab.meaning: The study of how drugs and chemicals affect cellular function in the nervous system and brain.
When a molecule binds to a protein at a special site to change its shape and boost its activity.
The process where a damaged nerve fiber actively chops itself up and destroys its own axon.
Medical damage or disease that is real and happening inside the body, but hidden beneath standard testing thresholds.

quiz.question: Why do an abnormally high percentage of patients with schizophrenia smoke cigarettes?
options: Purely out of boredom in hospitals
To unconsciously self-medicate a microscopic communication glitch in their brain's receptors
Because tobacco companies specifically target them
quiz.explanation: Nicotine targets specific acetylcholine receptors that temporarily help force their broken cognitive circuits to fire properly.

quiz.question: What determines whether a damaged nerve fiber (axon) decides to regenerate or destroy itself?
options: A chemical suicide switch governed by cellular energy molecules like NAD+
How fast the person's heart is beating
Whether the person is sleeping or awake
quiz.explanation: Proteins like SARM1 act as molecular executioners that trigger axon self-destruction when energy supplies drop too low.

quiz.question: What is 'subclinical' damage in the context of blast-mediated traumatic brain injury?
options: Damage that only appears on basic X-rays
Hidden cellular and visual damage that standard medical exams miss until it's too late
An injury that heals itself within five minutes
quiz.explanation: Subclinical damage operates beneath the radar of traditional imaging, requiring advanced diagnostic tools to catch a crucial treatment window.
